blocks.text: Ever popped a balloon? That bang is air pushing outward, hard and fast. A car engine is a machine that makes that push happen **thousands of times a minute** and turns it into a spinning shaft.
Here's the whole job in one line: **burn fuel, make hot gas, let the gas push a piston, turn the push into spin.**

blocks.caption: A single-cylinder engine, cut open. Tap pause any time.
blocks.narration: Watch the piston slide up and down inside the cylinder, while the crankshaft at the bottom spins round and round.

items: **Cylinder:** a tube. Everything happens inside it.
**Piston:** a plug that slides up and down in the tube.
**Connecting rod:** links the piston to the crankshaft.
**Crankshaft:** the bent shaft at the bottom. It turns up-and-down into round-and-round.
**Intake valve:** a door that lets air and fuel in.
**Exhaust valve:** a door that lets burnt gas out.
**Spark plug:** makes a tiny lightning bolt to light the fuel.

blocks.title: Everyday example
blocks.text: Pedalling a bike is the same trick. Your legs push **down** in a straight line, and the pedal cranks turn that into a **circle**. The crankshaft is the engine's pedal crank.

The piston goes up, then down, then up again. Each trip from the very top to the very bottom (or back) is called a **stroke**. The very top is **top dead centre**, the very bottom is **bottom dead centre**. At those points the piston stops for an instant before turning around.

blocks.title: Why "4-stroke"?
blocks.text: It takes **four** strokes to do the full job once: let the fuel in, squeeze it, burn it, push it out. That's the next lesson.

blocks.question: Which part turns the piston's up-and-down motion into spinning?
blocks.explain: The crankshaft does it, just like bike pedal cranks turn your legs' push into a circle.

blocks.question: What is one "stroke"?
options: One full turn of the crankshaft
One trip of the piston from top to bottom, or bottom to top
blocks.explain: A stroke is one trip of the piston between top dead centre and bottom dead centre. Two strokes = one crank turn.
